scope: Creative AI; October 12 weekly edition with dated October 13–16 deltas. New October 15 ResStreamGS paper and TaoMate FL2VA release. Retained records keep their original verification details; this is not an independent SOTA ranking. Excludes robotics and physical AI.

papers.title: ResStreamGS: stop sending the whole scene every frame.
papers.full_title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.summary: Caches stable splats per frame group; updates attribute-sensitive splats frame by frame.
papers.change: October 15 submission, after the previous review.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: six 300-frame sequences, held-out cameras, 20-frame groups. Against a controlled V3-style baseline: +7.51–8.35 dB PSNR and 21.4–56.5% lower amortized payload. 30.883 FPS on one Snapdragon 778G phone.
papers.caveat: Payload is not wireless performance. Culling and pruning also improve speed. Abrupt changes challenge fixed groups; GIFStream has smaller payloads.
papers.access: Full paper reviewed; implementation not verified, no reproduction.
papers.creator_implication: For captured volumetric scenes. Stationary splats can still need appearance updates.
papers.review_depth: Primary methods, evaluation, ablations and submission history.

papers.title: TaoMate FL2VA: keep the endpoint in view.
papers.summary: A public rank-128 adapter adds three-step blockwise first/last-frame control to the TaoMate H3 runtime.
papers.change: October 15 adapter release, confirmed by Hugging Face history. The linked July paper and September T2AV release are older.
papers.evaluation: One published FL2VA example and eight-GPU recipe. The model card speed table measures the older T2AV path; it is not an FL2VA benchmark.
papers.caveat: The inspected FL2VA recipe uses frozen teacher audio and whole-clip decoding. Streaming latent generation does not establish end-to-end live playback. No independent quality or speed test.
papers.access: Adapter files and inference source verified. Requires H3 base weights; MiniMax community license. No download or inference run.
papers.creator_implication: Interesting for shot endpoints and continuity. A converted LoRA alone does not provide the runtime cache or scheduling.
papers.review_depth: Model card, file history, official README and FL2VA inference/student source inspected.

papers.title: PLEDGE: decide what your splats are allowed to lose.
papers.full_title: PLEDGE: Progressive Lossy Error-Bounded Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.summary: A training-free progressive codec converts position, footprint, color and opacity tolerances into per-splat quantization bounds over a declared camera domain.
papers.caveat: Bounds are relative to the pruned model. Footprints use affine rasterization; composited color bounds require fixed geometry and opacity. This is not a guarantee on every final pixel.
papers.change: October 13 v1, newly discovered October 14 after arXiv listings advanced. Submission predates the previous review; discovery closes its documented coverage gap.
papers.evaluation: Authors test 13 scenes: nine Mip-NeRF 360, two Tanks and Temples, two Deep Blending. All 585 parameter checks satisfy bounds; smaller files at 11 of 19 comparable training-free baseline operating points. Not a universal compression winner.
papers.access: Paper methods and evaluation inspected. Public code, weights and executable demo not verified; no codec run.
papers.creator_implication: Useful for streaming 3D scenes with explicit distortion budgets. Proposed graphic: quantization error under camera changes, with scope of the guarantee visible.
papers.review_depth: Primary full-paper method, evaluation and limitation review; submission history verified; no reproduction

papers.title: PhysicsSliders: moving a sound is not the same as hitting its target.
papers.full_title: PhysicsSliders: Learning Physical Controls for Audio Foley Generation
papers.summary: A 54.8M flow transformer learns 15 controls from simulated contact sounds, with a frozen Stable Audio Open decoder. Separate variants take physical parameters or numerical captions.
papers.caveat: Sustained sounds cover a compressed target range. Effective damping depends on measurement, and controls interact. Perceptual evaluation remains future work.
papers.change: Submitted October 13, newly discovered in October 14 listings. This is recent Foley research missed during the previous listing-access gap, not a new October 14 submission.
papers.evaluation: Real-audio target tests cover 240 requests across five datasets and three training runs. A separate joint-control grid covers 225 setting–run evaluations: supplying thickness yields 68.0% success versus 27.6% when masked. Success requires at least two of four outputs within 1.5× of both eight-output simulator-median targets.
papers.access: Full paper inspected; code, weights and demo not verified. No audio generation or listening test performed.
papers.creator_implication: A concrete sound-design story: the controls omitted from a prompt can matter as much as those supplied. Proposed synthetic resonances expose the coupling.
papers.review_depth: Primary method, target protocol and limitations; submission history verified; no reproduction

papers.title: Drama 3: give the voice a little direction.
papers.summary: A new TTS release with plain-language direction and word-scoped delivery tags. The public model card describes a 35B-parameter mixture of experts with about 3B active per token and hybrid attention.
papers.caveat: Hosted take revision and audio inpainting are invite-only; the editing API is forthcoming. Open weights have commercial restrictions. Three billion active parameters does not mean the full model fits in 3B-sized memory.
papers.change: Released October 13, after the weekly cutoff. TTS is available through Fish Audio web, mobile and API; OpenArt also lists it, with its exact integration time unverified.
papers.evaluation: Fish reports a leading Artificial Analysis English pronunciation result. That human-rated difficult-span test does not establish best acting, multilingual quality or overall TTS leadership. Numeric ranking was not independently reverified here. No listening study or inference run performed.
papers.access: Public code and weights. Official installation specifies at least 48 GB GPU memory in FP8 and NVIDIA only. Community License v1.0 has an aggregate affiliate revenue threshold below US$500,000 for eligible commercial use and separate hosted-service terms; consult the actual LICENSE rather than stale Hub metadata.
papers.creator_implication: A timely voice-direction candidate for scripted dialogue. Check the exact model header: the vendor docs say a missing or misspelled header silently falls back to S2.1 Pro.
papers.review_depth: Release, model card, API docs, installation and license inspected; benchmark scope checked; no full technical-report audit or reproduction

papers.title: OuroWorld: make the scene loop, not just the video.
papers.full_title: OuroWorld: Bringing Any 3D World Alive as Diverse, Endlessly Looping 3D Cinemagraphs
papers.summary: Fits generated multi-view motion to periodic 4D Gaussians. A Fourier deformation field enforces loop closure; a reference-anchored drift field absorbs inconsistent training views.
papers.caveat: Loop closure does not guarantee plausible motion. Wider viewpoints expose inconsistent supervision; evaluation covers a limited orbit, not arbitrary free navigation.
papers.change: New to the watchlist: submitted 8 October, v1. Official implementation now inspected; no model execution.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation on 39 reconstructed/generated scenes, static and ±20° orbit cameras, ground-truth-free metrics and a 30-participant study against four baselines.
papers.access: Public code and run instructions verified. README says its code is MIT but the full pipeline includes non-commercial dependencies. The default reference-video path uses paid APIs; released references and a documented Wan 2.2 alternative are options. Weights and complete runs not tested.
papers.creator_implication: A useful direction for looping backgrounds and animated 3D set pieces. Periodic deformation offers a concrete graphic without presenting a synthetic demonstration as generated footage.
papers.review_depth: Primary full-paper method, evaluation and limitations; current submission history and official repository; no reproduction

papers.title: SepGen: keep the sounds on separate tracks.
papers.full_title: SepGen: Multi-Stem Audio-Video Separation and Generation in a Single Model
papers.summary: Adds captioned audio stems to a frozen joint audio-video generator, using stem-only LoRA updates and one-way attention from the protected scene mix to stems.
papers.caveat: Trained and evaluated for two sources. Stems retain scene acoustics and resynthesized phase; the spatial demo does not establish accurate source localization or new-view acoustics.
papers.change: New to the watchlist: submitted 8 October, v1. Official inference/training repository and checkpoint links inspected; no model execution.
papers.evaluation: 194 generated two-source prompts; separation on 149 Veo scenes, 64 LTX-2.3 scenes and 172 real SAM-Audio-bench recordings. Author-reported tests.
papers.access: Public inference/training code, HF adapter links and moving-camera demo verified. README requires a 48GB NVIDIA GPU and gated LTX-2.5 access; LTX-2.x Community License applies. Precomputed training features remain pending in the README; complete training-data availability not established.
papers.creator_implication: Separate dialogue or effects can be remixed after generation. Its repository includes a CrossView-Warp IC-LoRA/depth/stereo demonstration; treat that as a demo rather than validated spatial reconstruction.
papers.review_depth: Primary full-paper method, benchmarks, ablations and limitations; current history and official repository; HF checkpoint links followed but detailed retrieval intermittent; no reproduction

papers.title: Tabula Rasa: the noise can carry the camera move.
papers.full_title: Tabula Rasa: Monte Carlo estimation of unit-variance noise with controlled spatio-temporal correlation
papers.summary: Estimates projected Gaussian noise and its variance together, preserving geometry-linked temporal correlation through filtering.
papers.caveat: Finite sampling and histogram collisions introduce bias. Controlled correlation does not guarantee the generated scene obeys every geometric detail.
papers.change: New paper, submitted 8 October. Official JAX and WebGPU implementations inspected.
papers.evaluation: Author tests include noise statistics, rendering timing and 50 DAVIS super-resolution videos over five seeds; not a general video-generation ranking.
papers.access: Public facebookresearch repository includes JAX, mesh-based WebGPU demo and setup instructions. Majority licensed CC-BY-NC, with separate third-party licenses. No execution.
papers.creator_implication: A concrete route from camera motion to coherent noise; an unusually strong teaching topic about why ordinary noise warping changes variance.
papers.review_depth: Primary methods, statistical analysis, evaluation, bias discussion and official repository; no reproduction
